item.title: Bellingham beauty in Real Madrid win; Arsenal, Man City held in Champions League
item.description: Jude Bellingham scored one of the goals of the season as Real Madrid hammered PSV Eindhoven 5-1 on Tuesday to maintain their perfect record in this season’s Champions League, while Arsenal and Manchester City were both held to draws at home. Elsewhere, debutants Como and Real Betis continued their excellent form since the start of the league phase, but Aston Villa slumped to another defeat on their travels. Record 15-time European champions Real had to come from behind to beat PSV at the Bernabeu as they made it five wins from five in this season’s league phase to go clear at the top of the standings with 15 points. Dutch champions PSV led at half-time courtesy of an Ivan Perisic penalty, but Federico Valverde equalised five minutes after the restart. Bellingham then put Real ahead on the hour with a remarkable strike, as he controlled a Kylian Mbappe lay-off outside the box and then teed himself up for a sweet volley on the outside of his right boot which flew into the corner of the net. Mbappe then scored twice to move to 19 goals in all competitions this season and 76 career Champions League goals. The France captain now has 105 Real Madrid goals, one more than the Brazilian Ronaldo managed for the club. Vinicius Junior sealed the win for Jose Mourinho’s side, who have now claimed 10 consecutive victories in all competitions. “That one was a nice one, it popped up for me nicely and then I just hit it. I thought I would go with the outside of the boot a little bit, stab it a little bit, I am not one for smashing the ball too hard. It was a nice moment,” England star Bellingham told British broadcaster TNT Sports about his goal. Reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain can join Real at the top of the standings if they beat Roma on Wednesday, but Como and Betis are currently level with the French side on 12 points after they beat AEK Athens and Slovan Bratislava respectively. Como and Betis flying Luis Milla scored as Como beat AEK 1-0 in Italy after Lucas Da Cunha earlier squandered a penalty, while Cucho Hernandez grabbed both goals for Betis in their 2-0 victory in Slovakia. Arsenal had to settle for a point after drawing 1-1 with Borussia Dortmund at the Emirates Stadium, as Viktor Gyokeres put the Gunners ahead but later missed a golden chance to win the game. Gyokeres opened the scoring with a thunderous strike, but Maximilian Beier equalised for Dortmund and the Arsenal striker headed woefully wide from Martin Odegaard’s cross late on. It is the second time Arsenal, last season’s beaten finalists, have dropped points to German opposition this season following a 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich. Manchester City are in the midst of a poor run of form in the Premier League and Enzo Maresca’s side had to come from behind twice in the second half to draw 2-2 against Napoli. item.title: Trump, NATO chief to meet amid Ukraine security concerns
item.description: United States President Donald Trump is scheduled to meet NATO Secretary-General, Mark Rutte, today, amid growing concerns over European security and the ongoing war between Russia and Ukraine. The meeting, expected to take place in Palm Beach, Florida, comes as Washington and its European allies continue discussions over the future of Ukraine, military support and security guarantees for the war-torn country. According to Reuters, the White House announced the planned meeting, while NATO also confirmed Rutte’s visit to the United States. The discussions are expected to focus on transatlantic security relations, NATO’s defence commitments and efforts to find a diplomatic solution to the conflict between Moscow and Kyiv. Trump has repeatedly called on European members of NATO to increase their defence spending and take greater responsibility for the security of the continent. The meeting also comes amid disagreements among Western allies over the terms of a possible peace agreement and the extent of future military assistance to Ukraine. Rutte has maintained that NATO’s support for Ukraine remains important to European security, as Russia’s invasion continues to shape diplomatic and military calculations across the region. The outcome of Wednesday’s meeting could provide further indications of Washington’s position on NATO’s future role in the Ukraine conflict. item.title: Police declare 9 wanted over parcel of bullets sent to First Bank MD
item.description: The police have declared nine persons wanted over an alleged threat to the life of First Bank of Nigeria Ltd. Managing Director, Mr. Olusegun Alebiosu. The Assistant Inspector-General of Police (AIG), Zone 2, Mr Olohundare Jimoh, disclosed this on Tuesday in Lagos. Jimoh spoke while briefing journalists at the Zone 2 Police Command headquarters, Onikan. He said the threat involved a parcel containing two rounds of 7.62mm live ammunition delivered to Alebiosu’s residence. The parcel, packaged as a fashion-design gift, was delivered by a dispatch rider whose identity remained unknown. He said the incident was reported to the police on May 7, while the parcel was opened the following morning. Jimoh described the ammunition as dangerous, noting that the 7.62mm rounds were designed for compatible firearms, including AK-47 rifles. He said the discovery prompted a discreet investigation to identify those behind the alleged threat. A joint team of crime detectives, ballistic experts and forensic investigators was subsequently constituted to investigate the incident. According to him, preliminary investigations revealed that First Bank had undertaken extensive loan recovery activities involving customers allegedly owing several billions of naira. Some of the customers reportedly confronted bank representatives and issued threats against the managing director during the recovery process. Jimoh said the investigation was intended to establish the facts and identify those responsible for the alleged threat. He disclosed that 10 bank customers and other persons considered relevant to the investigation had been invited for questioning. The AIG said the invitations were issued in accordance with established investigative procedures and relevant legal provisions. He said the investigation complied with the Judges’ Rules, the 1999 Constitution, the Administration of Criminal Justice Act, 2015, and other applicable laws. Jimoh said the Firearms Act prohibited unlawful possession or control of ammunition without appropriate legal authorisation. He disclosed that the 10 persons were invited on Nov. 5 to appear for questioning on Nov. 12. However, only one person honoured the invitation, while the remaining nine failed to report. Consequently, the police declared the nine persons wanted to facilitate the investigation into the alleged threat against Alebiosu and his family. Jimoh urged anyone with useful information about their whereabouts to report to the nearest police station. He assured the public that the investigation would remain discreet and professional, adding that anyone found culpable would face the full weight of the law. The AIG stressed that nobody was above the law and that the police would ensure justice was served. He added that the rights of both the suspects and the complainant would be protected throughout the investigation. item.title: Governor Lawal shares 2,000 vehicles, tricycles, motorcycles
item.description: Governor Dauda Lawal said that distributing empowerment assets to beneficiaries shows his administration’s commitment to helping individuals and associations across Zamfara grow their businesses, create jobs, and become self-reliant. On Saturday, the governor launched the distribution of motorcycles, Keke NAPEP tricycles, Hijet pickups, and three-wheel barrow pickups to Zamfara residents at the Trade Fair Complex in Gusau, the state capital. The distribution is the second phase of the state government’s empowerment programme targeting various groups, organisations and associations through the Zamfara State Agency for Poverty Alleviation (ZAPA). The second phase includes 1,000 motorcycles, 1,000 tricycles popularly known as Keke NAPEP, 40 Hijet pickup vehicles, 40 three-wheeled pickup vehicles and 40 vehicles. In his remarks, Governor Lawal reiterated that the initiative offers another opportunity for prospective beneficiaries to expand their economic opportunities and improve their standard of living. He said, “This gathering is particularly important as it gives me a unique opportunity to formally distribute these vehicles in recognition of the immense contributions of individuals and various organisations to the overall development of our State. “I wish to commend the Zamfara State Agency for Poverty Alleviation (ZAPA) for its commitment to implementing this laudable initiative. “I also urge all beneficiary associations to regard these assets as valuable economic investments, utilise them strictly for their intended purposes and ensure timely repayment in accordance with the agreed loan arrangements. This will ensure the programme’s sustainability and enable other deserving citizens to benefit. “Let me remind this gathering that humanitarian services save lives, relieve suffering and protect human dignity during conflicts, natural disasters and health emergencies. They bridge immediate survival needs with long-term community recovery when local systems are overwhelmed. “My administration will continue to provide empowerment opportunities and livelihood support to individuals, groups and communities to expand opportunities and enhance the well-being of citizens of the State.” The post Governor Lawal shares 2,000 vehicles, tricycles, motorcycles appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Zamfara panel to review salaries of varsities, colleges
item.description: The Zamfara State Government yesterday inaugurated a committee to review and address the non-implementation of revised salary structures and other staff welfare issues in the state-owned tertiary institutions. The Secretary to the State Government and Chairman of the Committee, Malam Abubakar Mohammad Nakwada, inaugurated the committee and chaired its maiden meeting in Gusau, the state capital. The committee was expected to examine relevant government circulars towards addressing all outstanding welfare concerns of staff in the institutions. It will also determine financial implications and funding requirements involved, and consult relevant stakeholders to facilitate amicable resolution. Speaking at the inauguration, Mr Nakwada reaffirmed the administration’s commitment to staff welfare, industrial harmony, and the repositioning of tertiary education in the state. He further emphasised that Governor Dauda Lawal has proven to be workers-friendly, citing the upward review of the minimum wage from paltry N7,000 to N70,000, the clearing of the backlog of gratuities, the implementation of a new salary scale for healthcare workers, and other welfare commitments of the current administration. “This assignment is a clear demonstration of Governor Lawal’s commitment to the welfare of workers, industrial harmony, and the development of our tertiary institutions. “The demands presented by the Forum of Zamfara State Tertiary Institutions (FOZASTI) and the Zamfara State University on salary, allowances and promotion benefits have been a source of concern. The government considers it necessary to address these issues holistically, fairly and sustainably. “Our assignment must be guided by objectivity, sincerity, and the best interest of the State. We must listen to all parties, examine the facts and figures dispassionately, and come up with recommendations that are implementable, affordable and just. “I assure the staff unions and management of our institutions that this Government is not unmindful of their plight. At the same time, we must also be mindful of the financial realities of the state. “Our goal is to find a lasting solution that will guarantee industrial peace and improve the quality of education in Zamfara State,” the SSG stated. item.title: 2027: KDI records 124 attacks, 22 deaths ahead of polls
item.description: 53 days to elections, group warns of escalating political violence By John Alechenu, Abuja ABUJA — The Kimpact Development Initiative (KDI) has raised the alarm over escalating political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections, disclosing that its monitoring has recorded 124 incidents and 22 deaths across 35 states and the Federal Capital Territory between July 1 and November 23, 2026. The organisation warned that the growing incidents of violence and intimidation could undermine the credibility of the elections if urgent measures were not taken to address the situation. KDI released the figures on Tuesday under its Nigeria Election Violence Education and Reporting (NEVER) Project, 53 days before the January 16, 2027 presidential and National Assembly elections. According to the organisation, incidents of electoral violence increased sharply following the commencement of political campaigns, rising from three cases in July to 48 in October, while 40 incidents were recorded in the first half of November alone. “The overall trajectory suggests that electoral competition is becoming increasingly accompanied by violence and intimidation. If left unchecked, these trends could intensify further as election day approaches,” KDI said. The organisation noted that political violence was no longer restricted to traditionally identified hotspots, with Kano, Delta, Rivers, Edo, Ondo and Kebbi recording significant incidents, while several other parts of the country were also affected. Breaking down the incidents, KDI said physical assaults accounted for 46.8 per cent of reported cases, property destruction 28.8 per cent, shootings 10.2 per cent, intimidation and harassment nine per cent, and kidnappings four per cent. It also expressed concern over the growing use of hostile rhetoric, threats and inflammatory statements across political party lines, warning that such language could normalise violence and embolden supporters. The organisation identified political party members and affiliated groups as perpetrators in 82.3 per cent of the recorded incidents, while members of political parties were victims in 86.5 per cent of the cases. “Political leaders must take concrete measures to discourage violence, sanction supporters who engage in unlawful conduct, and publicly demonstrate their commitment to peaceful elections,” it said. KDI also raised concerns over growing political intolerance, including restrictions on opposition activities, alleged abuse of administrative authority and denial of equal opportunities to campaign. On accountability, the organisation said that despite several arrests reported since January, it had found no publicly available evidence of corresponding prosecutions or convictions in many of the cases. “This accountability deficit weakens deterrence and can create the perception that perpetrators of electoral violence can act with impunity,” it warned. item.title: Zamfara gov’t suspends campaign after road crash
item.description: The Zamfara government has suspended its scheduled campaign activities in Maru Local Government Area following a road accident that killed 15 APC supporters. The victims died along the Gummi-Daki-Takwas-Anka route while travelling to Talata Mafara for the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign rally. The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) confirmed that 15 people died, while 27 others sustained injuries in the crash. The accident occurred at about 12.30 p.m. on Monday near Kisami village, along the Gummi-Daki-Takwas-Anka route. The government announced the suspension in a statement issued by the Commissioner for Information and Culture, Mahmud Dantawasa, on Monday in Gusau. Dantawasa said the accident involved APC members travelling from Gummi Local Government Area. “The government expresses its deep sorrow over the unfortunate incident and extends its heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families,” he said. He also extended condolences to the Gummi Emirate and the APC family in Zamfara over the loss. The commissioner said the government sympathised with the injured and prayed for their speedy recovery. “In this moment of grief, the Zamfara State Government stands in solidarity with the affected families and all those mourning the loss of their loved ones,” he said. He urged residents to remain calm and offer prayers for the deceased and injured. “May Almighty Allah forgive the souls of the departed, grant them Aljannatul Firdaus, and give their families the strength and patience to bear this irreparable loss,” Dantawasa said. item.title: Ebonyi govt approves 933.777 hectares for smart city, dredging of 3.3km Ebonyi River against flooding
item.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The Ebonyi State Government has approved the establishment of a 933.777-hectare of new city called FON Smart City in Abakaliki, alongside the dredging of 3,305.61 metres of the Ebonyi River as part of measures to expand the state capital and mitigate potential flooding. The approvals were granted by the State Executive Council (EXCO), presided over by Governor Francis Ogbonna Nwifuru, during its meeting. The Commissioner for Information and State Orientation, Chief Ikeuwa Omebeh ehike briefing journalists on the outcome of the Exco meeting, said the proposed smart city would be developed on an additional 933.777 hectares of land acquired from the former Army land within Abakaliki capital. Omebeh explained that the council had approved the designation of the newly acquired territory and its entire development layout as FON Smart City, Abakaliki. He said the initiative was part of the Nwifuru administration’s strategic urban development agenda aimed at expanding the territorial boundaries of the state capital, attracting private-sector investments and stimulating economic activities. According to him, the proposed smart city has been designed with clearly defined land-use zones to accommodate the state’s growing residential, commercial, institutional and developmental requirements. He listed the components of the master plan to include residential neighbourhoods, institutional zones, commercial districts, a Central Business District, green verges, agricultural and farming zones, community resettlement areas and special provision areas. The commissioner said the carefully structured development framework was intended to create a modern urban environment capable of accommodating future population growth while improving the infrastructural capacity, aesthetics and economic outlook of Abakaliki. He added that the project would open up new investment opportunities, expand economic activities and strengthen Ebonyi State’s position as an emerging investment destination in the South-East. Also, the State Executive Council approved the dredging of approximately 3,305.61 metres (3.3 kilometres) of the Ebonyi River to address potential flooding threats within sections of the proposed smart city. Omebeh said the decision followed the identification of flood-prone areas within the proposed development corridor, necessitating proactive environmental intervention to safeguard the planned urban infrastructure. He explained that the dredging exercise would improve water flow, reduce flooding risks and provide the necessary environmental protection for the sustainable development of the new city. The commissioner stressed that the government’s decision to incorporate flood-control measures into the smart city project underscored its commitment to sustainable urban planning and the protection of public infrastructure against environmental hazards. item.title: Surgeons offer free knee replacements as orthopaedic association begins AGM
item.description: … Over 100 patients receive free treatment in Abuja outreach By Ruth Onyekachi No fewer than 100 people living with disabling bone and joint conditions received free medical attention on Monday as Nigerian orthopaedic surgeons began a three-day surgical outreach in Abuja, offering procedures, including costly knee replacements, to patients who cannot afford them. The outreach, organised by the Nigerian Orthopaedic Association (NOA) as part of activities marking its 49th Annual General Meeting (AGM) and Scientific Conference, will run until Wednesday across five hospitals in the Federal Capital Territory. The participating facilities are Wuse District Hospital, Garki Hospital, Federal Medical Centre, Abuja, Cedarcrest Hospital and Alliance Hospital, where orthopaedic surgeons drawn from across the country are providing consultations, surgeries and post-operative care at no cost to beneficiaries. For many of the patients, the intervention represents an opportunity to access procedures that would ordinarily cost millions of naira, particularly knee replacement surgeries that remain beyond the reach of low-income Nigerians. Vice President of the association, Dr Christian Madubueze, who represented its President, Dr E.A. Orimolade, said the outreach was part of NOA’s commitment to making specialised orthopaedic care accessible to underserved Nigerians. “This is not the first time we have done an outreach with the FCT — we did one during our 2023 AGM that was hosted here, and we were very happy, we were well treated, and we were able to serve patients,” he said. He disclosed that the association would undertake a significant number of knee replacement operations free of charge. “We are doing a significant number of knee replacement surgeries which normally would have cost these patients millions of naira, but we as an association are going to do them here,” he explained. Madubueze said the choice of established hospitals was deliberate because complex procedures such as joint replacement require standard operating theatres and specialised facilities. “It is actually not possible for us to be doing this in the villages unless we are going to set up a makeshift hospital there, which will dramatically increase the cost,” he said, adding that “Wuse District Hospital is very important to us.” The FCT administration also welcomed the initiative, describing it as an important intervention for residents who struggle to access specialised medical services. Director of Clinical Services, Dr Osayande Osagie, who represented the Mandate Secretary for Health Services and Environment, Dr Adedolapo Fasawe, said the administration appreciated the association for bringing the services closer to the people. “Orthopaedic surgery or consultations are not things that are cheap to find, especially in a town like Abuja,” Osagie said. “This corporate social responsibility that you brought to the people of Abuja, we really appreciate it, and on their behalf I want to say a big

item.title: Nigerian children: Millions still face barriers to education, protection
item.description: …Demand free education, stronger safeguards, greater voice in decisions By Chioma Obinna For millions of Nigerian children, the promise of a safe childhood, quality education and a future shaped by their dreams remains a daily struggle. From access to basic education and healthcare to protection from abuse and poverty, the gap between children’s rights and their lived realities continues to raise concerns about the country’s commitment to its youngest population. The challenge came into focus on Friday as the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) and the Lagos State Government marked the 2026 World Children’s Day, calling for stronger protection of children’s rights and concrete government action to secure their future. At the celebration, held at the UNICEF Lagos Office under the theme, “My Day. My Rights. My Future,” children demanded free education, greater protection and a stronger voice in decisions affecting their lives. UNICEF Chief of Field Office, Lagos, Celine Lafoucriere, warned that children’s rights were increasingly under threat globally, stressing that governments and other stakeholders must do more to guarantee access to education, healthcare, good nutrition, clean water, sanitation and social protection. “Children’s rights are under pressure, they’re under threat, they’re being increasingly threatened throughout the world,” she said. She noted that recognising children’s rights was not enough if families and communities lacked the resources to make those rights meaningful. Lafoucriere explained that social protection programmes were essential to helping vulnerable children access basic services, particularly education, healthcare and adequate nutrition. “Having a right is one thing, but it’s not going to put food on the table,” she said. She stressed that UNICEF was working with the Lagos State Government to ensure that children’s rights were respected and accessible to every child, particularly those from vulnerable backgrounds. “The child is the future, and the future of Nigeria is today,” she declared, urging society to recognise that investment in children could not be postponed. Children want more than promises Beyond the concerns raised by development partners and government officials, the celebration provided an opportunity for children to articulate their expectations of those responsible for protecting their rights. The Speaker of the Lagos State Children’s Parliament, Rt. Hon. Abdulsalam Anjola, called for greater involvement of children in decisions affecting their welfare, insisting that their experiences and opinions must count when policies concerning them are formulated. He said children were often better positioned to explain the challenges they faced, particularly cases of abuse and other threats to their safety. item.title: Political Signals: The Price Of Participation
item.description: Deadly violence in Delta sharpens the question of campaign safety, while economic policy and electoral preparations face tests. An election campaign should ask citizens for their votes. In Uduere, Delta State, families are now mourning people who went to a political gathering. Police said on Tuesday that six people died in Monday’s violence at a campaign event in Ughelli North. That preliminary figure is higher than the four deaths initially reported by Ovie Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation. The circumstances and responsibility remain under investigation. This is the most consequential political development since Friday. Its significance extends beyond one party’s campaign. Every attack raises a question for the next person considering attending a meeting, volunteering or accompanying a candidate: is participation worth the risk? When citizens begin making that calculation, electoral competition has already suffered. Delta Needs Evidence And Accountability Delta Governor Sheriff Oborevwori The NDC has alleged official complicity. The Delta State Government has rejected attempts to link Governor Sheriff Oborevwori to the violence, condemned the killings and promised that those responsible will face justice. Those competing positions must remain distinct from investigative findings. The state has imposed a daily 6 p.m. to 6 a.m. curfew across Ughelli North. Restoring calm is an immediate necessity. Establishing responsibility is the next obligation. The investigation should establish the sequence of events, identify those who used weapons and examine allegations about the conduct of officials and security personnel. Witnesses need protection, and the public needs credible updates. Political leaders also have an immediate responsibility to restrain inflammatory claims and prevent retaliation. The standard is straightforward: lawful political activity must receive protection regardless of the party organising it. A Separate Court Decision Changes The Delta Contest On Tuesday, the Federal High Court in Warri nullified Omo-Agege’s nomination as the NDC’s Delta Central senatorial candidate and directed INEC to remove his name. Reporting attributes the decision to failures concerning the party’s membership register and nomination requirements. Responses from Omo-Agege and the NDC were unavailable in the initial reports. The ruling and Monday’s violence are separate matters. Their proximity establishes no connection between them. Ovie Omo-Agege Electorally, however, the judgment creates fresh uncertainty around an influential politician and the organisation supporting him. Any subsequent appeal, interim order and INEC action will matter. The wider lesson reaches across party lines: recruitment and defections must be supported by lawful nomination procedures. Political prominence cannot resolve defective paperwork. item.title: Nigeria Is Cutting The Budget, But Not The Deficit
item.description: The economic signal this week is that the Federal Government has acknowledged that its 2026 budget is larger than it can credibly implement. President Bola Tinubu has asked the National Assembly to repeal and re-enact the 2026 Appropriation Act, reducing total expenditure from ₦68.323 trillion to ₦65.176 trillion, a cut of approximately ₦3.15 trillion, or 4.6 per cent. Budget revision is not inherently a sign of failure. Governments should adjust spending plans when revenue, financing conditions or obligations change. An unrealistic budget does not become credible merely because it has been signed into law. The more important signal is what remains unchanged: a ₦31.457 trillion fiscal deficit and planned new borrowing of ₦29.218 trillion. Nigeria is reducing expenditure, but it is not reducing the gap between what government earns and what it intends to spend. What Is Being Revised Under the proposed framework, projected federal revenue, including receipts from government-owned enterprises, stands at ₦33.720 trillion. Capital expenditure is estimated at ₦26.232 trillion, while the deficit remains equivalent to 5.64 per cent of GDP. The borrowing plan comprises ₦18.428 trillion in domestic financing and ₦10.790 trillion from external sources. The government says its proposed $7.7 billion foreign loan will fund an existing external-borrowing provision rather than increase the approved envelope. President Bola Tinubu signed into law the Appropriation (Amendment) (No.4) Bill, 2025, on September 30, 2026. The administration says the revision will regularise expenditure incurred by NNPC Limited on behalf of the Federation, address debt-service obligations that were underprovided for, recognise already issued capital warrants and supplementation commitments, and refund ministries and special accounts. Some new allocations are also proposed for critical roads, agriculture, farm productivity, market access and water security. These may be legitimate obligations. But their late recognition exposes weaknesses in the original budget’s preparation. The Credibility Problem The 2026 budget began as an executive proposal of approximately ₦58.47 trillion. It was subsequently expanded and signed at ₦68.323 trillion in April. Seven months later, the executive is asking Parliament to reduce it. The new figure remains ₦6.7 trillion above the original proposal. This sequence matters because Nigeria’s budget has become less a binding financial plan than a collection of ambitions, negotiated additions and subsequent corrections. Ministries receive large appropriations but often wait months for releases. Projects are announced without complete financing. Unpaid obligations accumulate and eventually return as supplementary provisions. A smaller, executable budget would be preferable to a larger one that exists chiefly on paper. item.title: 2027: Omo-Agege Not A Threat, Can’t Get 25% Of Votes For Obi – Delta Council Chairman
item.description: The Chairman of Ughelli North Local Government Council in Delta State, Jaro Egbo, has dismissed former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege as a political threat ahead of the 2027 general elections, insisting that the former lawmaker lacks the support to secure significant votes for the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the state. Egbo said Omo-Agege would struggle to deliver even 25 per cent of the votes for the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, arguing that his political influence in Delta State was exaggerated. The council chairman spoke on Tuesday as a guest on Channels Television’s ‘Politics Today’, where he was asked whether Omo-Agege’s claim that the APC could not win elections in Delta State was a source of concern, particularly given Obi’s victory in the state during the 2023 presidential election. Responding, Egbo questioned Omo-Agege’s political strength, recalling that the former deputy senate president was a member of the All Progressives Congress during the 2023 elections but could not secure 25 per cent of the votes for President Bola Tinubu in Delta State. “When Peter Obi contested and won in Delta in 2023, Omo-Agege was in APC. Omo-Agege couldn’t get 25 per cent of the vote for Mr President. If he was that popular, why was he unable to get 25 per cent for Mr President?” he asked. ﻿ Egbo, who said he belonged to the Peoples Democratic Party at the time, added that his party secured more than 25 per cent of the votes for its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar. He argued that Omo-Agege’s defection to the NDC would not translate into electoral gains for Obi, insisting that the former deputy senate president lacked the political following to influence the outcome of the election. “Now that he has gone to NDC, I am sure he won’t be able to also get 25 per cent for Peter Obi. So, he’s not a threat to anybody. He knows that he’s not a threat,” he said. Egbo, who is also from Ughelli North, Omo-Agege’s hometown, urged Omo-Agege to face the electorate rather than make claims about his political strength, saying voters would determine his popularity at the polls. Egbo also called on the former deputy senate president to tone down his political rhetoric. Omo-Agege had, during an appearance on Politics Today on Monday, dismissed the APC’s chances of winning elections in Delta State in 2027, citing Obi’s popularity and the support base he claimed to command. “Peter Obi remains very popular here in Delta State. There is no chance that APC will win anything,” he said. Omo-Agege, who left the APC for the NDC in May 2026, also argued that a combination of his political support base and Obi’s popularity would make it difficult for the ruling party to win in the state. Egbo, who Omo-Agege accused of masterminding an alleged assassination attempt against him, denied the allegation while speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Tuesday. ﻿ He alleged that the senator’s supporters fired the first shots during the senator’s campaign visit, triggering anger among residents. The chairman said he was not present at the venue and was at his office at the time of the incident. Egbo dismissed Omo-Agege’s claim that he was targeted for assassination. He, however, expressed condolences to victims on both sides, irrespective of their political affiliations. Meanwhile, the Delta State Police Command has invited the former deputy senate president and the Ughelli North Local Government Chairman and five others for questioning over the deadly attack on the NDC campaign convoy. ﻿ The post [VIDEO] NDC: Delta LG Chairman Claims Ughelli Attack Was A Reprisal appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Police Invite Omo-Agege, Delta Council Chairman, Five Others Over Attack In Ughelli
item.description: The Delta State Police Command has invited a former deputy senate president, Ovie Omo-Agege, Ughelli North Local Government Chairman Jaro Egbo and five others for questioning over the deadly attack on a campaign convoy of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the state. The police said the invitations were part of an ongoing investigation into the violence that occurred during an NDC campaign in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area, on Monday. In a statement issued on Tuesday, the Police Public Relations Officer, Bright Edafe, said the invited individuals had been asked to report to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) at the police headquarters in Asaba on specified dates. Omo-Agege, the NDC senatorial candidate for Delta Central, is expected to appear on Thursday at 11 a.m., while Egbo has been invited for 2 p.m. on the same day. The five other invitees are Gowon Egoide, a former chairman of Uduere Quarters; Onoriode Oneya, the incumbent youth chairman of Uduere Community; Edirin Wokode Ewhubare, an associate of Egoide; Erukaye Egoide, Egoide’s nephew; and Tony Gabon Mevowovo, another associate of Egoide. Photo of a Nigerian Police They are expected to appear before the police on Friday, November 27, at noon. The police said the invitations were intended to establish the individuals’ level of involvement in the incident. The development comes as Governor Sheriff Oborevwori, accompanied by the Commissioner of Police, Samuel Erale, and other heads of security agencies, visited Uduere community for an on-the-spot assessment of the attack. During the visit, the governor expressed confidence in the police command to ensure that everyone found culpable was brought to justice, irrespective of political affiliation or status. ﻿ The Commissioner of Police urged the invited individuals to honour the invitations and cooperate with investigators. He also warned that the command would not accept the presence of supporters or other persons who had not been formally invited. The police assured residents that the investigation would be thorough and impartial, adding that anyone found culpable would be brought to justice. The command also appealed to residents to remain calm and law-abiding as investigations continue. ﻿ Meanwhile, Omo-Agege and Egbo have traded conflicting accusations over who orchestrated the attack. The attack left six people dead, according to preliminary police reports, while several others sustained injuries. Omo-Agege reportedly escaped unhurt. item.title: CBN Retains Interest Rate At 23% As Inflation Drops To 14.06%
item.description: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has retained its Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) at 23 per cent, despite a further decline in the country’s inflation rate to 14.06 per cent in October 2026. The decision was taken at the 308th meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), held on Monday and Tuesday, November 23 and 24, 2026. In a communiqué issued on Tuesday and signed by the CBN Governor, Olayemi Cardoso, the committee also retained the Standing Facilities Corridor at +50/-300 basis points around the MPR. It further maintained the Cash Reserve Requirement (CRR) for Deposit Money Banks at 45 per cent, Merchant Banks at 16 per cent and non-Treasury Single Account (TSA) public sector deposits at 75 per cent. The committee said the decision was informed by the need to sustain the progress made in reducing inflation and keep inflation expectations under control. ﻿ It noted that headline inflation had moderated for five consecutive months, supported by exchange rate stability and improved transmission of monetary policy measures. However, members expressed concern over prevailing economic headwinds that could slow the pace of the decline in price pressures, maintaining that the current monetary policy stance remained appropriate. According to the CBN, headline inflation declined to 14.06 per cent in October from 14.63 per cent in September 2026. Core inflation also dropped to 10.78 per cent from 12.95 per cent, while food inflation eased to 19.13 per cent from 19.59 per cent over the same period. The committee attributed the moderation in food inflation to lower prices of processed food and farm produce following the commencement of the harvest season. It also noted that the composite Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rose to 53.2 points in October from 53.0 points in September, indicating sustained expansion in economic activities across the industrial, agricultural and services sectors. The CBN said Nigeria’s gross external reserves stood at $54.02bn as of November 17, 2026, providing cover for 10.26 months of imports of goods and services. Inflation Risks View of a market area in Osun State, Nigeria. Despite the improvement in key economic indicators, the MPC identified potential risks that could put renewed pressure on prices. These include the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, which could sustain elevated global energy prices, as well as increased spending associated with the end-of-year festive season and election-related activities. The committee also expressed confidence that continued exchange rate stability and improved food supply would support the disinflation process. It welcomed a Memorandum of Understanding between the CBN and the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited, aimed at boosting foreign exchange inflows, supporting energy project financing and improving macroeconomic stability. item.title: [VIDEO] 2027 Elections: Everybody Should Be Allowed To Campaign Freely, Says Obi
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has called on the Federal Government and security agencies to ensure that all political parties and candidates are allowed to campaign freely ahead of the 2027 general elections, condemning the growing incidents of political violence across the country. Speaking to Channels Television after interacting with residents during a town hall meeting in Taraba State, the former Anambra State governor described the situation as unhealthy for Nigeria’s democracy. Obi was responding to questions about the reported attack on the campaign convoy of his party’s Delta Central senatorial candidate, Ovie Omo-Agege, and concerns over the safety of opposition politicians. ﻿ He said there was no justification for subjecting Nigerians to violence during political campaigns, stressing that the country should uphold peaceful democratic practices. Obi also urged the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to allow a free, fair and credible electoral process, noting that the party already controls the government. Beyond politics, Obi said his town hall engagements were aimed at listening to Nigerians and understanding their challenges, including unemployment, overtaxation of small businesses, lack of access to funding, strikes in schools and inadequate primary healthcare. He described listening to citizens as an essential part of responsible and demand-driven leadership.
